The field is prefilled 0.1.0, read from package.json in the pod, and validates: typing "nope" showed "A version has to be major.minor.patch, for example 0.2.0." and disabled Publish; typing 0.3.0 changed the hint to "Publishing rewrites that file to 0.3.0." The write is real - with the file writable, publishing with 0.4.0 in the box left `"version": "0.4.0"` in the pod's package.json. Restored to 0.1.0. Worth knowing: when the write cannot happen the dialog says nothing and publishes anyway. package.json in barn-base-extension is root-owned while the exec runs as uid 1000, so two of my attempts left the file at 0.1.0 with no error shown and the dialog closing normally - writeExtensionFile goes through podExecOnce, which resolves with whatever stdout it saw and never surfaces a non-zero exit or stderr, and writeVersion never re-reads to confirm.

It also is not "the only unticked one": this dialog pre-ticks nothing, so all five rows start unticked. The row states why: "There is no SUSE catalog reachable from this environment and no submission for this Studio to make, so there is nothing behind this box."
